met_analysis:
The Depression over Jharkhand and adjoining Gangetic West Bengal moved west-northwestwards with a speed of 18 kmph during past 6 hours and lies centered at 0830 hrs IST of today, the 14th August, 2026, over the same region, near latitude 23.2°N and longitude 85.5°E, about 20 km southeast of Ranchi (Jharkhand), 80 km west-northwest of Jamshedpur (Jharkhand), 90 km south of Hazaribagh (Jharkhand), 170 km east-southeast of Daltonganj (Jharkhand) and 230 km east of Ambikapur (Chhattisgarh). It is very likely to continue to move west- northwestwards across Jharkhand & north Chhattisgarh and weaken into well marked low pressure area during next 12 hours.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Firozpur, Muzaffarnagar, Fatehgarh, Daltonganj, centre of Depression over Jharkhand and adjoining Gangetic West Bengal and Digha & thence southeastwards to Eastcentral Bay of Bengal.
The Shear Zone runs roughly along Lat. 23°N across central & adjoining north Peninsular India between 3.1 & 7.6 km above mean sea level tilting southwards with height.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northwest Madhya Pradesh & neighbourhood extending upto 5.8 km above mean sea level and tilting southwards with height merged with the Shear Zone.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle and upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level runs roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over northwest Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhoodat 0.9 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over southwest Rajasthan adjoining Pakistan between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level.
A north-south trough runs from northwest Rajasthan to northeast Arabian sea across Gujarat at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
